problem_motivation.content: Fabrication-induced extrinsic disorder obscures intrinsic localization and degrades transport in ReS2.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, extrinsic disorder caused by fabrication methods obscures inherent localization behavior arising from reduced dimensionality and degrades transport properties.

problem_motivation.content: Intrinsic Anderson localization in 2D semiconductors has been hard to quantify experimentally because fabrication disorder dominates transport.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Despite extensive investigation, quantitative experimental access to intrinsic Anderson localization in 2D semiconductors has been severely limited by extrinsic disorder introduced during device fabrication, which dominates transport and obscures intrinsic localization behavior.

prior_approach.content: Prior reports observed 2D Mott VRH in several 2D semiconductors.
prior_approach.evidence_span: 2D Mott VRH has been reported in MoS2,6–11 WS2,12,13 MoSe2,14 WSe2,15 and BP16–18 with extracted localization lengths varying widely depending on sample quality and dielectric environment.

prior_approach.content: ReS2 has previously been used as the channel in FETs with reported mobility and on/off ratios.
prior_approach.evidence_span: ReS2 has been incorporated as the channel material in field-effect transistors (FETs)31–33, exhibiting n-type transport with room-temperature field-effect mobilities up to 30 cm²V-1s-1,33 and on/off ratios exceeding 10^6,34.

prior_approach.content: A conductance dome had been reported previously in electrolyte-gated few-layer ReS2.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The partial rather than complete conductance suppression at high gate voltages is similar to the conductance dome reported in electrolyte-gated few-layer ReS₂29.

prior_approach.content: Hopping transport with increasing mobility versus temperature has been seen in other localized 2D semiconductor FETs.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The monotonic increase of µ with T is consistent with hopping transport observed in other localized 2D semiconductor FETs7.

prior_approach.content: In wider-band TMDs like MoS2 and WS2, EF crosses the mobility edge and a metal-insulator transition occurs.
prior_approach.evidence_span: This behavior is absent in wider-band TMDs such as MoS2 and WS2, where  𝐸𝐹 crosses the mobility edge within experimentally accessible gate voltage ranges, producing a metal-insulator transition6,12,45.

prior_approach.content: Devices were assembled using a standard sequential all-dry transfer method.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Top-gated van der Waals heterostructure FETs were assembled by sequential all-dry transfer [1]

prior_limitation.content: Prior ReS2 devices suffered interface charge trapping that obscured intrinsic localization.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, in these devices, significant interface charge trapping introduces extrinsic disorder that dominates transport and obscures the intrinsic localization behavior of ReS2

rejected_alternative.content: Unlike prior electrolyte-gated work where ionic gate disorder could contribute, this study rules that out and treats the feature as intrinsic.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: In   the present top-gated device, the absence of ionic gate disorder establishes this feature as intrinsic to the ReS₂ band structure.

rejected_alternative.content: The authors explicitly rule out gate-induced disorder as the explanation for non-monotonic Ea.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: In the present top-gated device gate-induced disorder is ruled out as a contributing factor, unambiguously establishing the non-monotonic 𝐸𝑎 as an intrinsic consequence of the narrow ReS2 conduction band.

causal_claim.content: All-dry assembly removes fabrication contamination, and hBN suppresses interface trapping that previously prevented intrinsic localization measurements.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The all-dry assembly eliminates fabrication-induced contamination at the channel interfaces, while the atomically flat, trap-free hBN dielectric suppresses interface charge trapping that had prevented characterization of intrinsic Anderson localization in ReS2.

causal_claim.content: Graphene source-drain electrodes reduce Schottky barrier height and contact resistance.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Few-layer graphene (FLG) layers are used as source–drain electrodes which reduce the Schottky barrier height and contact resistance at the metal–semiconductor junction36,37.

causal_claim.content: hBN provides a flat low-trap interface.
causal_claim.evidence_span: A hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) flake (~10.0 nm thickness, measured by AFM, SI S3) serves as the gate dielectric, providing an atomically flat interface with minimal charge traps and dangling bonds38

causal_claim.content: Transparent FLG top gate enables efficient electrostatic control through thin hBN.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Transparent FLG is used as the top gate, enabling efficient electrostatic control through the thin hBN dielectric39,40.

causal_claim.content: The order-of-magnitude hysteresis contrast shows dielectric interface quality controls charge trapping and validates the clean platform.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The order-of-magnitude contrast in hysteresis between the two devices establishes dielectric interface quality as the decisive factor controlling charge trapping in ReS2 FETs, and validates the top-gated device as a clean platform for investigating intrinsic Anderson localization.

causal_claim.content: Lower temperatures progressively localize carriers, shifting threshold voltage positively.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Transfer characteristics at selected temperatures (Fig. 2(c)) show a systematic positive shift of the threshold voltage (Vth) from ≈ 0.5 V at 200 K to ≈ 2.7 V at 4 K, reflecting the progressive localization of carriers at low temperatures.

causal_claim.content: Positive temperature coefficient and low mobility indicate localization rather than phonon-limited band transport.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This behavior, combined with the low mobility values, confirms that transport is governed by intrinsic carrier localization arising from the narrow ReS2 conduction bandwidth, rather than band-like conduction45.

causal_claim.content: As gate voltage increases below 2.8 V, EF moves toward EC and activation energy decreases.
causal_claim.evidence_span: For Vg < 2.8 V, EF moves through the band-tail states toward 𝐸𝐶, reducing 𝐸𝑎 monotonically by ~10 meV.

causal_claim.content: The finite minimum in Ea at 2.8 V means EF gets closest to EC without crossing it.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The finite minimum at Vg ≈ 2.8 V establishes that EF reaches its closest approach to 𝐸𝐶 without crossing it.

causal_claim.content: Above 2.8 V, high DOS below EC resists further EF movement, collapsing gate efficiency and raising Ea.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Above Vg = 2.8 V, EF enters the high-DOS region below 𝐸𝐶, where the large number of states per unit energy resists further EF movement, causing gate efficiency to collapse and 𝐸𝑎 to rise ~1 meV toward Vg = 4 V, consistent with the conductance suppression observed in Fig. 2(c).

causal_claim.content: T0 decreases with gate voltage because EF moves through band-tail states toward EC, weakening localization.
causal_claim.evidence_span: 𝑇0 decreases monotonically from ~1 ×104 K at Vg = 1 V to ~10 K at Vg = 4 V (Fig. 4(b)), consistent with the progressive movement of 𝐸𝐹  through the band-tail states toward 𝐸𝐶 and the systematic weakening of carrier localization with increasing gate voltage.

causal_claim.content: Breakdown of both NNH and VRH analyses above 4 V indicates EF has entered the high-DOS region below EC.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The simultaneous breakdown of both the NNH Arrhenius analysis and the VRH fits above Vg = 4 V confirms that 𝐸𝐹 has entered the high-DOS region immediately below 𝐸𝐶, consistent with the band-tail structure established in the previous section.

causal_claim.content: This difference shows van der Waals interface engineering is necessary to access intrinsic Anderson localization.
causal_claim.evidence_span: directly demonstrating that van der Waals interface engineering is essential for accessing the intrinsic Anderson localization in ReS2.

causal_claim.content: Van der Waals interface engineering with hBN enabled intrinsic Anderson localization that is inaccessible in contaminated, trap-dominated devices.
causal_claim.evidence_span: In summary, we have demonstrated intrinsic Anderson localization in few-layer ReS2 field-effect transistors through van der Waals interface engineering with hBN gate dielectric, inaccessible in devices where fabrication-induced contamination and interface charge trapping dominate transport.

causal_claim.content: The results show van der Waals interface engineering is essential for revealing intrinsic quantum transport in narrow-band 2D semiconductors.
causal_claim.evidence_span: These results demonstrate that van der Waals interface engineering is essential for uncovering intrinsic quantum transport in narrow-band 2D semiconductors.

causal_claim.content: Negligible hysteresis indicates gate-induced disorder does not affect intrinsic localization.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The hysteresis is negligible (ΔV < 0.1 V) at 4 K confirming that gate-induced disorder does not affect the intrinsic localization.

causal_claim.content: Mean free path much smaller than the Re-Re bond length confirms strong localization.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the mean free path 𝑙 ≈ 0.02 nm, more than one order of magnitude smaller than the Re–Re bond length (0.28 nm), confirming the system is in the strongly localized regime.

causal_claim.content: Near-threshold conductance scatter and noise-floor approach cause large uncertainty in T0 at 1 V.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The large uncertainty in 𝑇0 at 𝑉𝑔 = 1V arises from increased conductance scatter within the 10 –100 K fitting window near threshold, where the exponentially suppressed conductance approaches the noise floor, reducing the precision of the VRH fit.

causal_claim.content: Monotonic decrease of T0 with gate voltage is caused by progressive filling of localized band-tail states.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The monotonic decrease of 𝑇0 with gate voltage across the full range, despite the large uncertainty at the lowest gate voltage, is physically consistent with progressive filling of localized band-tail states

mechanism_principle.content: Reduced dimensionality means weak disorder can localize all states in 2D semiconductors.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Carrier localization governs low-temperature transport of two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors, where reduced dimensionality makes even weak disorder sufficient to localize all electronic states for non-interacting electrons1,2.

mechanism_principle.content: VRH reflects phonon-assisted tunnelling between localized states.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The hallmark transport signature of Anderson localization is variable-range hopping (VRH)3,4, reflecting phonon-assisted tunnelling between spatially localized states.

mechanism_principle.content: At higher temperature, thermal energy activates nearest-neighbor hopping.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: At higher temperatures, nearest-neighbor hopping (NNH)5 dominates as thermal energy becomes sufficient to activate transitions between adjacent localized sites, yielding thermally activated conductance.

mechanism_principle.content: Peierls-distorted ReS2 has a narrow conduction bandwidth, making the disorder-to-bandwidth ratio large enough to localize carriers.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: ReS2 crystallizes in a distorted 1T structure arising from Peierls distortion19, which gives rise to pronounced in-plane anisotropy20–28, and produces an exceptionally narrow conduction bandwidth29,30, making the disorder-to-bandwidth ratio sufficiently large to localize carriers throughout the band and rendering ReS2 particularly susceptible to carrier localization.

mechanism_principle.content: Hysteresis in the SiO2 device comes from charge trapping at the interface and in defect-rich amorphous SiO2.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: arising from charge trapping at the ReS2/SiO2 interface and within the amorphous SiO2 dielectric, which contains a high density of dangling bonds, oxygen vacancies, and defect sites42–44.

mechanism_principle.content: In few-layer 2D channels, hysteresis is mainly controlled by the gate dielectric interface, not thickness.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: However  , hysteresis in few-layer 2D channels is primarily governed by the gate dielectric interface rather than the channel thickness41,42.

mechanism_principle.content: High-gate-voltage conductance suppression is due to collapse of gate efficiency when EF enters high-DOS band-tail states below the mobility edge.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This suppression reflects the collapse of gate efficiency as Fermi energy (𝐸𝐹) enters the high-DOS region of the band-tail below the mobility edge (𝐸𝐶).

mechanism_principle.content: The effect is intrinsic to ReS2 because of its narrow conduction bandwidth.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This is an intrinsic feature of the narrow ReS2 conduction bandwidth29,30, discussed in the following section.

mechanism_principle.content: The non-monotonic activation energy comes from narrow-bandwidth ReS2 with disorder strong enough to localize carriers throughout the band.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This non-monotonic gate-voltage dependence reflects the transport physics of the narrow ReS2 conduction bandwidth (D ∼0.4 eV)29, which makes the disorder strength W/D sufficiently large to localize carriers throughout the band.

mechanism_principle.content: Very small kF*l signifies strong localization where quantum interference dominates over semiclassical transport.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The Ioffe–Regel parameter 𝑘𝐹∗𝑙 defines the transport regime, with 𝑘𝐹∗𝑙≪ 1 indicating the strongly localized (Anderson insulating) regime where quantum interference dominates over semiclassical transport.

hypothesis_statement.content: Eliminating fabrication disorder and suppressing interface trapping should reveal intrinsic Anderson localization in ReS2.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We report intrinsic Anderson localization in few-layer ReS2 by eliminating extrinsic fabrication-induced disorder through all-dry van der Waals assembly and suppressing interface charge trapping through a hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) gate dielectric.

hypothesis_statement.content: All-dry transfer with hBN dielectric and graphene electrodes can create a clean platform to study intrinsic Anderson localization.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Here, we report temperature-dependent transport in few-layer AA-stacked ReS2 FETs fabricated by all-dry transfer on pre-patterned electrodes, with hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) as the top-gate dielectric and few-layer graphene (FLG) source, drain, and gate electrodes.

hypothesis_statement.content: Below the crossover, transport is described by 2D Mott VRH.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Below 𝑇∗ ≈ 100 K, transport is governed by 2D Mott VRH,

hypothesis_statement.content: The low-temperature transport mechanism is proposed/tested as either 2D Mott VRH or ES-VRH, with identification of the operative one.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: VRH models were evaluated against the low-temperature conductance data (T < 𝑇∗(𝑉𝑔)) to identify the operative transport mechanism. Two models were tested, 2D Mott VRH [9] and Efros–Shklovskii (ES) VRH [10].

evidence_result.content: Temperature-dependent transport shows a crossover from nearest-neighbor hopping to 2D Mott VRH.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Temperature-dependent transport reveals a crossover from nearest-neighbor hopping to two-dimensional (2D) Mott variable-range hopping (VRH).

evidence_result.content: Non-monotonic activation energy versus gate voltage enables access to the energy-resolved band-tail DOS.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The non-monotonic gate-voltage dependence of activation energy provides direct access to the energy-resolved band-tail density of states of the ReS2 conduction band.

evidence_result.content: 2D Mott VRH gives an intrinsic localization length much larger than in disorder-dominated devices.
evidence_result.evidence_span: 2D Mott VRH yields a localization length of (3.5 ± 0.1) nm, an order of magnitude larger than disorder-dominated devices, providing a quantitative characterization of intrinsic Anderson localization in ReS2.

evidence_result.content: Negligible hysteresis versus SiO2 back-gated devices confirms suppression of interface disorder.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Negligible gate hysteresis, compared to back-gated devices with SiO2 dielectric fabricated from the same source crystal, confirms the effective suppression of interface disorder.

evidence_result.content: Transport shows a gate-dependent crossover from NNH to 2D Mott VRH while remaining Anderson insulating.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Transport measurements reveal a gate-dependent crossover from thermally activated NNH to 2D Mott VRH, with both regimes confined entirely within the Anderson insulating regime across the accessible gate voltage and temperature range.

evidence_result.content: Above the crossover, activation energy versus gate voltage gives direct access to band-tail structure.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Above the crossover, the activation energy exhibits a non-monotonic gate-voltage dependence, providing direct experimental access to the energy-resolved band-tail structure of the narrow ReS2 conduction band.

evidence_result.content: Top-gated hBN device shows negligible hysteresis, confirming suppressed charge trapping.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The device exhibits n-type behavior with negligible hysteresis (ΔV < 0.1 V) between forward and reverse gate voltage sweeps, directly confirming the suppression of charge trapping at the ReS2/hBN interface, consistent with the low intrinsic trap density of hBN dielectrics41,42.

evidence_result.content: SiO2 back-gated comparison device shows strong hysteresis.
evidence_result.evidence_span: This device exhibits pronounced hysteresis (ΔV ≈ 45 V)

evidence_result.content: Conductance is suppressed as temperature decreases across all gate voltages.
evidence_result.evidence_span: revealing an overall suppression of conductance with decreasing temperature across all gate voltages.

evidence_result.content: A crossover occurs near 100 K: high-T NNH and low-T VRH.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The temperature dependence of conductance on a semi-log scale (Fig. 2(b)) reveals a crossover at 𝑇∗ ≈ 100 K. Above 𝑇∗, conductance decreases strongly and monotonically with decreasing temperature at all gate voltages, characteristic of thermally activated nearest-neighbor hopping (NNH). Below 𝑇∗, the temperature dependence weakens and becomes strongly gate-voltage-dependent, indicating a crossover to variable-range hopping (VRH) transport.

evidence_result.content: Arrhenius fits in the high-temperature regime have high R2 and confirm the crossover temperature.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Linear fits (solid lines) in the NNH regime (Fig. 3(b)) yield 𝑅2 ≥ 0.98 across all gate voltages, confirming 𝑇∗≈ 100 K as the crossover temperature.

evidence_result.content: Below the crossover the data deviate from Arrhenius behavior, indicating VRH.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Below 𝑇∗(orange region), the data deviate systematically from Arrhenius linearity, signalling a crossover to VRH transport.

evidence_result.content: The system stays in the Anderson insulating regime over the full gate range.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Throughout the entire gate range, the Ioffe–Regel parameter 𝑘𝐹∗𝑙≪ 1 (SI S5), confirming that the system remains in the Anderson insulating regime.

evidence_result.content: Within the reliable window, extracted DOS plateaus and matches the theoretical 2D DOS.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Within this window, 𝑔(𝐸𝐹) plateaus at (2.06 ± 0.04) × 1014 eV−1 cm−2, in agreement with the theoretical 2D DOS

evidence_result.content: High R2 in VRH plots confirms 2D Mott VRH as the operative mechanism.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The curves exhibit higher 𝑅2 across all gate voltages [SI S6], confirming 2D Mott VRH as the operative transport mechanism, consistent with the finite DOS at 𝐸𝐹 established earlier.

evidence_result.content: Intrinsic localization length is 3.5 ± 0.1 nm and exceeds the Re-Re bond length.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The intrinsic localization length, extracted as the weighted mean over Vg = 1–2.1 V, is (3.5 ± 0.1) nm, satisfying ξ ≫ a = 0.28 nm46 (Re–Re bond length).

evidence_result.content: Across all accessible gate voltages, transport crosses from NNH to 2D Mott VRH while remaining Anderson insulating.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Temperature-dependent transport reveals a gate-dependent crossover from thermally activated NNH to 2D Mott VRH, with both regimes confined entirely within the Anderson insulating regime across all accessible gate voltages.

evidence_result.content: Activation energy versus gate voltage provides direct experimental access to the band-tail DOS.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The non-monotonic gate-voltage dependence of the activation energy provides direct experimental access to the energy-resolved band-tail density of states of the ReS2 conduction band.

evidence_result.content: VRH analysis gives a localization length an order of magnitude larger than prior disorder-contaminated devices.
evidence_result.evidence_span: 2D Mott VRH analysis yields a localization length of (3.5 ± 0.1) nm, an order of magnitude larger than values from disorder-contaminated devices in prior reports.

evidence_result.content: Raman mode separation confirms AA-stacked ReS2.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The frequency separation between Mode I and Mode III is 12.8 cm⁻¹, as shown in Fig. S1(a), which is consistent with ~12 cm⁻¹ for AA-stacked ReS2 [2,3].

evidence_result.content: PL peak energies match literature values for AA-stacked few-layer ReS2.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Figure S1(b) shows two peaks corresponding to 𝑋1 and 𝑋2 excitons at (1.560 ± 0.002) eV and (1.596 ± 0.002) eV. These peaks are consistent with literature values reported for AA-stacked few-layer ReS2 [4,5].

evidence_result.content: Room-temperature I-V curves confirm ohmic transport.
evidence_result.evidence_span: FIG S3. Room temperature I-V characteristics of ReS2 FETs with (a) hBN dielectric and (b) SiO2 dielectric for different gate voltages, confirming ohmic transport at room temperature.

evidence_result.content: Low-temperature transfer curves show negligible hysteresis.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Figure S4 shows transfer characteristics of the hBN-gated device recorded at 4 K with forward and reverse gate sweeps at 20 mV/s. The hysteresis is negligible (ΔV < 0.1 V) at 4 K

evidence_result.content: 2D Mott VRH fits better than ES-VRH at every gate voltage.
evidence_result.evidence_span: 2D Mott VRH yields systematically higher R² than ES-VRH at all gate voltages, confirming it as the dominant hopping transport mechanism across the full gate range.

evidence_result.content: At 4 V, ES-VRH deviates more strongly from linearity than 2D Mott VRH.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Figure S6 illustrates the comparison at 𝑉𝑔 = 4 V, where the deviation of ES-VRH from linearity is most pronounced.

evidence_result.content: Intrinsic localization length is 3.5 ± 0.1 nm from the low-gate intrinsic regime.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The intrinsic localization length ξ = (3.5 ± 0.1) nm is extracted as the weighted mean over 𝑉𝑔= 1 –2.1 V, where 𝑇0/27 ≫ 4 K.

evidence_result.content: In the plateau region, quantum-capacitance correction to DOS is negligible at about 0.8%.
evidence_result.evidence_span: In the plateau region (1.2–1.8 V), the measured derivative is | ≈ 125 V/eV. The correction term (−1 in absolute units of V/eV) is therefore negligible. So, ∆𝑔𝑔 ⁄ = | 𝑑𝐸𝑎/𝑑𝑉𝑔| = 0.008 = 0.8%

constraint.content: Reliable DOS extraction is limited to a gate-voltage window where Ea changes smoothly and monotonically.
constraint.evidence_span: Reliable extraction is restricted to 1.2 V < Vg< 1.8 V, where 𝐸𝑎varies smoothly and monotonically; outside this window, particularly near Vg ≈ 2.8 V where extracted 𝑔(𝐸𝐹) diverges as a mathematical artifact of the vanishing derivative rather than reflecting a physical feature of the DOS.

constraint.content: Further increase in localization length at high gate voltage is only an upper bound because VRH self-consistency fails.
constraint.evidence_span: with further increase at higher gate voltages representing upper bounds due to VRH self-consistency violation (SI S7)

constraint.content: Transport measurements were restricted to the linear ohmic regime.
constraint.evidence_span: All transport measurements are performed in the linear (ohmic) regime, where conductance 𝐺= 𝐼𝑑𝑠/𝑉𝑑𝑠 is independent of the applied bias.

constraint.content: The VRH fitting temperature window depends on gate voltage and is bounded by crossover temperature and noise floor.
constraint.evidence_span: The VRH fitting window varies with gate voltage. At all gate voltages, the upper bound is set by 𝑇∗ ≈ 100 K. The lower bound is 10 K for 𝑉𝑔 < 2.5 V, where conductance approaches the noise floor at lower temperatures, and extends to 4 K for 𝑉𝑔 ≥ 2.5 V, where the conductance remains measurable above the noise floor.

constraint.content: Physical validity of 2D Mott VRH requires hopping distance to exceed localization length, equivalent to T < T0/27.
constraint.evidence_span: A necessary condition for the physical validity of 2D Mott VRH is that the optimal hopping distance 𝑅ℎ𝑜𝑝 exceeds the localization length ξ.

constraint.content: If the self-consistency criterion is violated, the extracted localization length is only an upper bound.
constraint.evidence_span: When this criterion is violated, the VRH description breaks down; the extracted ξ then represents an upper bound.

constraint.content: For gate voltages at or above 3.3 V, all extracted localization lengths are only upper bounds because self-consistency fails over the accessible temperature range.
constraint.evidence_span: For 𝑉𝑔 ≥ 3.3 V, 𝑇0/27 falls below the lowest accessible measurement temperature (T = 4 K), meaning the self-consistency criterion 𝑇0/27 > T is violated at every measured data point. The corresponding ξ values are therefore upper bounds

constraint.content: The simplified DOS expression is valid only when geometric capacitance dominates quantum capacitance.
constraint.evidence_span: The density of states formula used in the main text (Eq. 2) is the simplified expression valid when the gate dielectric capacitance 𝐶ℎ𝐵𝑁 dominates over the quantum capacitance 𝐶𝑄 of the two-dimensional electron gas.

contradiction.content: The intrinsic localization length found here contrasts sharply with prior disorder-dominated reports.
contradiction.evidence_span: Below the crossover, 2D Mott analysis yields an intrinsic localization length in sharp contrast to prior reports from disorder-dominated devices29,34.

contradiction.content: The measured intrinsic localization length is far larger than prior ReS2 reports from disorder-dominated devices.
contradiction.evidence_span: The intrinsic localization length (3.5 ± 0.1) nm stands in sharp contrast to ξ ~ 0.35 nm29 from disorder-dominated devices, which is comparable to the Re–Re bond length (0.28 nm46)

problem_motivation.content: Quantitative experimental access to intrinsic Anderson localization in 2D semiconductors, including ReS2, has been severely limited because fabrication-induced extrinsic disorder dominates transport, obscures the material’s intrinsic localization behavior, and degrades transport properties.
evidence_spans: However, extrinsic disorder caused by fabrication methods obscures inherent localization behavior arising from reduced dimensionality and degrades transport properties.

Despite extensive investigation, quantitative experimental access to intrinsic Anderson localization in 2D semiconductors has been severely limited by extrinsic disorder introduced during device fabrication, which dominates transport and obscures intrinsic localization behavior.

prior_approach.content: Prior reports observed 2D Mott variable-range hopping in several 2D semiconductors, including MoS2, WS2, MoSe2, WSe2, and black phosphorus, with extracted localization lengths varying widely depending on sample quality and dielectric environment.
evidence_spans: 2D Mott VRH has been reported in MoS2,6–11 WS2,12,13 MoSe2,14 WSe2,15 and BP16–18 with extracted localization lengths varying widely depending on sample quality and dielectric environment.

prior_approach.content: ReS2 had previously been used as the channel material in field-effect transistors, showing n-type transport with room-temperature field-effect mobilities up to 30 cm²V-1s-1 and on/off ratios exceeding 10^6.
evidence_spans: ReS2 has been incorporated as the channel material in field-effect transistors (FETs)31–33, exhibiting n-type transport with room-temperature field-effect mobilities up to 30 cm²V-1s-1,33 and on/off ratios exceeding 10^6,34.

prior_approach.content: A conductance dome had previously been reported in electrolyte-gated few-layer ReS2, with only partial rather than complete conductance suppression at high gate voltages.
evidence_spans: The partial rather than complete conductance suppression at high gate voltages is similar to the conductance dome reported in electrolyte-gated few-layer ReS₂29.

prior_approach.content: In other localized 2D semiconductor FETs, hopping transport had been observed, consistent with mobility increasing monotonically with temperature.
evidence_spans: The monotonic increase of µ with T is consistent with hopping transport observed in other localized 2D semiconductor FETs7.

prior_approach.content: In wider-band TMDs such as MoS2 and WS2, EF can cross the mobility edge within experimentally accessible gate-voltage ranges, producing a metal-insulator transition.
evidence_spans: This behavior is absent in wider-band TMDs such as MoS2 and WS2, where 𝐸𝐹 crosses the mobility edge within experimentally accessible gate voltage ranges, producing a metal-insulator transition6,12,45.

prior_limitation.content: Prior ReS2 devices suffered from significant interface charge trapping, introducing extrinsic disorder that dominated transport and obscured the intrinsic localization behavior of ReS2.
evidence_spans: However, in these devices, significant interface charge trapping introduces extrinsic disorder that dominates transport and obscures the intrinsic localization behavior of ReS2

rejected_alternative.content: Gate-induced/ionic gate disorder is rejected as the explanation for the observed feature, including the non-monotonic activation energy Ea; instead, it is treated as intrinsic to the narrow ReS2 conduction band/band structure.
evidence_spans: In   the present top-gated device, the absence of ionic gate disorder establishes this feature as intrinsic to the ReS₂ band structure.

In the present top-gated device gate-induced disorder is ruled out as a contributing factor, unambiguously establishing the non-monotonic 𝐸𝑎 as an intrinsic consequence of the narrow ReS2 conduction band.

causal_claim.content: Van der Waals interface engineering using an all-dry assembled hBN dielectric creates a clean, atomically flat, low-trap interface by eliminating fabrication contamination and suppressing interface charge trapping; this clean platform is necessary to access and validate intrinsic Anderson localization in ReS2, which is otherwise inaccessible in contaminated, trap-dominated devices, and more broadly is essential for revealing intrinsic quantum transport in narrow-band 2D semiconductors.
evidence_spans: The all-dry assembly eliminates fabrication-induced contamination at the channel interfaces, while the atomically flat, trap-free hBN dielectric suppresses interface charge trapping that had prevented characterization of intrinsic Anderson localization in ReS2.
A hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) flake (~10.0 nm thickness, measured by AFM, SI S3) serves as the gate dielectric, providing an atomically flat interface with minimal charge traps and dangling bonds38

The order-of-magnitude contrast in hysteresis between the two devices establishes dielectric interface quality as the decisive factor controlling charge trapping in ReS2 FETs, and validates the top-gated device as a clean platform for investigating intrinsic Anderson localization.
directly demonstrating that van der Waals interface engineering is essential for accessing the intrinsic Anderson localization in ReS2.

In summary, we have demonstrated intrinsic Anderson localization in few-layer ReS2 field-effect transistors through van der Waals interface engineering with hBN gate dielectric, inaccessible in devices where fabrication-induced contamination and interface charge trapping dominate transport.
These results demonstrate that van der Waals interface engineering is essential for uncovering intrinsic quantum transport in narrow-band 2D semiconductors.

causal_claim.content: Few-layer graphene source-drain electrodes reduce Schottky barrier height and contact resistance at the metal-semiconductor junction.
evidence_spans: Few-layer graphene (FLG) layers are used as source–drain electrodes which reduce the Schottky barrier height and contact resistance at the metal–semiconductor junction36,37.

causal_claim.content: A transparent FLG top gate enables efficient electrostatic control through the thin hBN dielectric.

causal_claim.content: The systematic positive threshold-voltage shift on cooling indicates that lower temperatures progressively localize carriers.
evidence_spans: Transfer characteristics at selected temperatures (Fig. 2(c)) show a systematic positive shift of the threshold voltage (Vth) from ≈ 0.5 V at 200 K to ≈ 2.7 V at 4 K, reflecting the progressive localization of carriers at low temperatures.

causal_claim.content: The positive temperature coefficient together with low mobility indicates transport is governed by intrinsic carrier localization from the narrow ReS2 conduction bandwidth, rather than phonon-limited band-like transport.
evidence_spans: This behavior, combined with the low mobility values, confirms that transport is governed by intrinsic carrier localization arising from the narrow ReS2 conduction bandwidth, rather than band-like conduction45.

causal_claim.content: For Vg below about 2.8 V, increasing gate voltage moves EF through localized band-tail states toward EC, which decreases the activation energy Ea and weakens localization, as also reflected by the monotonic decrease in T0.
evidence_spans: For Vg < 2.8 V, EF moves through the band-tail states toward 𝐸𝐶, reducing 𝐸𝑎 monotonically by ~10 meV.

𝑇0 decreases monotonically from ~1 ×104 K at Vg = 1 V to ~10 K at Vg = 4 V (Fig. 4(b)), consistent with the progressive movement of 𝐸𝐹  through the band-tail states toward 𝐸𝐶 and the systematic weakening of carrier localization with increasing gate voltage.

The monotonic decrease of 𝑇0 with gate voltage across the full range, despite the large uncertainty at the lowest gate voltage, is physically consistent with progressive filling of localized band-tail states

causal_claim.content: The finite minimum in Ea at Vg ≈ 2.8 V indicates EF approaches EC most closely without crossing it.
evidence_spans: The finite minimum at Vg ≈ 2.8 V establishes that EF reaches its closest approach to 𝐸𝐶 without crossing it.

causal_claim.content: Above about 2.8 V, EF enters a high-density-of-states region just below EC; the large DOS resists further EF movement, collapses gate efficiency, and causes Ea to rise, while the breakdown of both NNH and VRH analyses above 4 V confirms entry into this high-DOS region.
evidence_spans: Above Vg = 2.8 V, EF enters the high-DOS region below 𝐸𝐶, where the large number of states per unit energy resists further EF movement, causing gate efficiency to collapse and 𝐸𝑎 to rise ~1 meV toward Vg = 4 V, consistent with the conductance suppression observed in Fig. 2(c).

The simultaneous breakdown of both the NNH Arrhenius analysis and the VRH fits above Vg = 4 V confirms that 𝐸𝐹 has entered the high-DOS region immediately below 𝐸𝐶, consistent with the band-tail structure established in the previous section.

causal_claim.content: Negligible hysteresis at 4 K indicates that gate-induced disorder does not affect the intrinsic localization.
evidence_spans: The hysteresis is negligible (ΔV < 0.1 V) at 4 K confirming that gate-induced disorder does not affect the intrinsic localization.

causal_claim.content: A mean free path much smaller than the Re-Re bond length confirms the system is in the strongly localized regime.
evidence_spans: the mean free path 𝑙 ≈ 0.02 nm, more than one order of magnitude smaller than the Re–Re bond length (0.28 nm), confirming the system is in the strongly localized regime.

causal_claim.content: Large uncertainty in T0 at Vg = 1 V is caused by increased near-threshold conductance scatter and the conductance approaching the noise floor within the fitting window, which reduces VRH fit precision.
evidence_spans: The large uncertainty in 𝑇0 at 𝑉𝑔 = 1V arises from increased conductance scatter within the 10 –100 K fitting window near threshold, where the exponentially suppressed conductance approaches the noise floor, reducing the precision of the VRH fit.

mechanism_principle.content: In 2D semiconductors, reduced dimensionality makes even weak disorder sufficient to localize all electronic states for non-interacting electrons; in ReS2, its Peierls-distorted structure produces an exceptionally narrow conduction bandwidth, so the disorder-to-bandwidth ratio is large enough to localize carriers throughout the band, making localization an intrinsic feature of the material.
evidence_spans: Carrier localization governs low-temperature transport of two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors, where reduced dimensionality makes even weak disorder sufficient to localize all electronic states for non-interacting electrons1,2.

ReS2 crystallizes in a distorted 1T structure arising from Peierls distortion19, which gives rise to pronounced in-plane anisotropy20–28, and produces an exceptionally narrow conduction bandwidth29,30, making the disorder-to-bandwidth ratio sufficiently large to localize carriers throughout the band and rendering ReS2 particularly susceptible to carrier localization.
This is an intrinsic feature of the narrow ReS2 conduction bandwidth29,30, discussed in the following section.

This non-monotonic gate-voltage dependence reflects the transport physics of the narrow ReS2 conduction bandwidth (D ∼0.4 eV)29, which makes the disorder strength W/D sufficiently large to localize carriers throughout the band.

mechanism_principle.content: Variable-range hopping is the hallmark transport signature of Anderson localization and reflects phonon-assisted tunnelling between spatially localized states; at higher temperatures, transport crosses over to nearest-neighbor hopping when thermal energy is sufficient to activate transitions between adjacent localized sites, yielding thermally activated conductance.
evidence_spans: The hallmark transport signature of Anderson localization is variable-range hopping (VRH)3,4, reflecting phonon-assisted tunnelling between spatially localized states.

At higher temperatures, nearest-neighbor hopping (NNH)5 dominates as thermal energy becomes sufficient to activate transitions between adjacent localized sites, yielding thermally activated conductance.

mechanism_principle.content: In few-layer 2D channels, hysteresis is governed mainly by the gate dielectric interface rather than channel thickness; for the SiO2 device specifically, it arises from charge trapping at the ReS2/SiO2 interface and within defect-rich amorphous SiO2 containing dangling bonds, oxygen vacancies, and other defect sites.
evidence_spans: However  , hysteresis in few-layer 2D channels is primarily governed by the gate dielectric interface rather than the channel thickness41,42.
arising from charge trapping at the ReS2/SiO2 interface and within the amorphous SiO2 dielectric, which contains a high density of dangling bonds, oxygen vacancies, and defect sites42–44.

mechanism_principle.content: High-gate-voltage conductance suppression arises because gate efficiency collapses when the Fermi energy enters the high-density-of-states band-tail region below the mobility edge.
evidence_spans: This suppression reflects the collapse of gate efficiency as Fermi energy (𝐸𝐹) enters the high-DOS region of the band-tail below the mobility edge (𝐸𝐶).

mechanism_principle.content: A very small Ioffe–Regel parameter (kF*l << 1) signifies the strongly localized Anderson-insulating regime, where quantum interference dominates over semiclassical transport.
evidence_spans: The Ioffe–Regel parameter 𝑘𝐹∗𝑙 defines the transport regime, with 𝑘𝐹∗𝑙≪ 1 indicating the strongly localized (Anderson insulating) regime where quantum interference dominates over semiclassical transport.

hypothesis_statement.content: Using an all-dry van der Waals device architecture with hBN dielectric and graphene electrodes to eliminate fabrication-induced disorder and suppress interface charge trapping should provide a clean platform that reveals intrinsic Anderson localization in few-layer ReS2.
evidence_spans: We report intrinsic Anderson localization in few-layer ReS2 by eliminating extrinsic fabrication-induced disorder through all-dry van der Waals assembly and suppressing interface charge trapping through a hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) gate dielectric.

Here, we report temperature-dependent transport in few-layer AA-stacked ReS2 FETs fabricated by all-dry transfer on pre-patterned electrodes, with hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) as the top-gate dielectric and few-layer graphene (FLG) source, drain, and gate electrodes.

hypothesis_statement.content: At low temperature below the crossover (T* ≈ 100 K), the operative transport mechanism is hypothesized/tested within variable-range hopping models, specifically distinguishing between 2D Mott VRH and Efros–Shklovskii VRH, with 2D Mott VRH identified as the appropriate description.
evidence_spans: Below 𝑇∗ ≈ 100 K, transport is governed by 2D Mott VRH,

VRH models were evaluated against the low-temperature conductance data (T < 𝑇∗(𝑉𝑔)) to identify the operative transport mechanism. Two models were tested, 2D Mott VRH [9] and Efros–Shklovskii (ES) VRH [10].

evidence_result.content: Temperature-dependent transport shows a gate-dependent crossover near T* ≈ 100 K from high-temperature thermally activated nearest-neighbor hopping (NNH) to low-temperature 2D Mott variable-range hopping (VRH); below T* the data deviate from Arrhenius behavior, 2D Mott VRH fits better than ES-VRH at all gate voltages, and both regimes remain entirely within the Anderson insulating regime across the accessible gate range.
evidence_spans: Temperature-dependent transport reveals a crossover from nearest-neighbor hopping to two-dimensional (2D) Mott variable-range hopping (VRH).

Transport measurements reveal a gate-dependent crossover from thermally activated NNH to 2D Mott VRH, with both regimes confined entirely within the Anderson insulating regime across the accessible gate voltage and temperature range.

The temperature dependence of conductance on a semi-log scale (Fig. 2(b)) reveals a crossover at 𝑇∗ ≈ 100 K. Above 𝑇∗, conductance decreases strongly and monotonically with decreasing temperature at all gate voltages, characteristic of thermally activated nearest-neighbor hopping (NNH). Below 𝑇∗, the temperature dependence weakens and becomes strongly gate-voltage-dependent, indicating a crossover to variable-range hopping (VRH) transport.
Linear fits (solid lines) in the NNH regime (Fig. 3(b)) yield 𝑅2 ≥ 0.98 across all gate voltages, confirming 𝑇∗≈ 100 K as the crossover temperature.
Below 𝑇∗(orange region), the data deviate systematically from Arrhenius linearity, signalling a crossover to VRH transport.
Throughout the entire gate range, the Ioffe–Regel parameter 𝑘𝐹∗𝑙≪ 1 (SI S5), confirming that the system remains in the Anderson insulating regime.
High R2 in VRH plots confirms 2D Mott VRH as the operative mechanism.
2D Mott VRH yields systematically higher R² than ES-VRH at all gate voltages, confirming it as the dominant hopping transport mechanism across the full gate range.
Figure S6 illustrates the comparison at 𝑉𝑔 = 4 V, where the deviation of ES-VRH from linearity is most pronounced.

Temperature-dependent transport reveals a gate-dependent crossover from thermally activated NNH to 2D Mott VRH, with both regimes confined entirely within the Anderson insulating regime across all accessible gate voltages.

evidence_result.content: 2D Mott VRH analysis yields an intrinsic localization length of (3.5 ± 0.1) nm, extracted in the low-gate intrinsic regime (Vg = 1–2.1 V), which is much larger than the Re–Re bond length and about an order of magnitude larger than in prior disorder-dominated/disorder-contaminated devices.

constraint.content: Transport measurements were restricted to the linear (ohmic) regime, where conductance is bias-independent.
evidence_spans: All transport measurements are performed in the linear (ohmic) regime, where conductance 𝐺= 𝐼𝑑𝑠/𝑉𝑑𝑠 is independent of the applied bias.

constraint.content: The VRH fitting temperature window is gate-voltage dependent and bounded above by the crossover temperature T* ≈ 100 K and below by the conductance noise floor/accessibility: 10 K for Vg < 2.5 V and 4 K for Vg ≥ 2.5 V.
evidence_spans: The VRH fitting window varies with gate voltage. At all gate voltages, the upper bound is set by 𝑇∗ ≈ 100 K. The lower bound is 10 K for 𝑉𝑔 < 2.5 V, where conductance approaches the noise floor at lower temperatures, and extends to 4 K for 𝑉𝑔 ≥ 2.5 V, where the conductance remains measurable above the noise floor.

constraint.content: Physical validity of 2D Mott VRH requires the optimal hopping distance to exceed the localization length, equivalently T < T0/27; when this self-consistency criterion is violated, the VRH description breaks down and the extracted localization length ξ should be treated only as an upper bound.
evidence_spans: A necessary condition for the physical validity of 2D Mott VRH is that the optimal hopping distance 𝑅ℎ𝑜𝑝 exceeds the localization length ξ.
When this criterion is violated, the VRH description breaks down; the extracted ξ then represents an upper bound.

constraint.content: At high gate voltage, especially for Vg ≥ 3.3 V, VRH self-consistency fails over the accessible temperature range, so any further increase in extracted localization length is only an upper bound.
evidence_spans: with further increase at higher gate voltages representing upper bounds due to VRH self-consistency violation (SI S7)

constraint.content: Reliable DOS extraction is limited to a gate-voltage window where Ea varies smoothly and monotonically, specifically about 1.2 V < Vg < 1.8 V; outside this range, especially near Vg ≈ 2.8 V, the extracted g(EF) can diverge as a mathematical artifact. In addition, the simplified DOS expression is valid only when the geometric gate capacitance dominates the quantum capacitance.

The density of states formula used in the main text (Eq. 2) is the simplified expression valid when the gate dielectric capacitance 𝐶ℎ𝐵𝑁 dominates over the quantum capacitance 𝐶𝑄 of the two-dimensional electron gas.)

contradiction.content: The intrinsic localization length measured here is much larger than prior ReS2 reports from disorder-dominated devices, sharply contrasting with those earlier disorder-dominated results.
evidence_spans: Below the crossover, 2D Mott analysis yields an intrinsic localization length in sharp contrast to prior reports from disorder-dominated devices29,34.
